text:
lina_support: FYI we have a high-severity from AcmePay. Their mobile client is hitting 429s in short bursts and the SDK retries are causing duplicate payment attempts. Customer reports duplicate charges after network blips. Attaching logs below.

mike_sre: Ugh. Do we have the call traces or header dumps? Need to see Retry-After, rate-limit headers, and the client retry pattern.

lina_support: Paste of 3 sample requests 
```
Request 1: POST /v1/charges 200 id=ch_ABC123 idempotency: none
Request 2: POST /v1/charges 429 Retry-After: 1
Request 3: POST /v1/charges 200 id=ch_DEF456 idempotency: none
```
The mobile SDK is using default retries (we think). Customer says requests 2/3 are within ~800ms.

jess_sdk: Quick context: our JS/Swift SDKs default to 3 retries with base backoff 300ms and exponential multiplier ~2, plus small jitter. Historically that reduces transient 5xx/timeout noise, but for 429s we expect clients to honor Retry-After and stop retrying non-idempotent endpoints unless an idempotency key is provided.

eli_infra: Also important: our burst window logic groups by customer org + route. If a client sends many retries quickly (no smoothing), they can blow through bursting quota and then get queued/429'd. That leads to a retry-fanout where SDK retries amplify the burst.

amy_billing: Customer is worried about duplicate billing. We should recommend idempotency keys for charge creations. We can also offer to refund duplicates if needed, but need repro for billing ops.

lina_support: Repro steps supplied by customer: 1) Start mobile app. 2) Toggle network off/on quickly. 3) Trigger payment flow twice. Observed two successes separated by a transient 429. They sent curl (redacted):
```
# Simulated: network blip + immediate retry
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/charges \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" \n  -d '{"amount":1000,"currency":"usd"}'
# client re-attempts after 300ms and 700ms -> duplicate payments
```

mike_sre: OK. Immediate actions: 1) Confirm server returned Retry-After header on 429. 2) Check logs for Idempotency-Key header presence. 3) Suggest SDK change to not automatically retry on 429 for POST /charges unless Idempotency-Key is present.

jess_sdk: Agreed. For non-idempotent POSTs we should default to 0 retries on 429/409 responses unless the app sets an Idempotency-Key header. Current behaviour (3 retries) is risky for payments. We can ship a minor SDK patch to change this default and add a louder warning in docs.

eli_infra: I'll look up the customer org's rate-limit resets. From logs: their X-RateLimit-Limit=60/min, X-RateLimit-Remaining was 2 then 0 within the burst. Server did include Retry-After: 2 on the 429.

jess_sdk: Proposed fix for SDK (short):
```
// pseudocode: retry policy for critical non-idempotent endpoints
if (method == POST && endpointMatchesCharge) {
  if (!headers.contains("Idempotency-Key")) {
    retries = 0
  } else {
    retries = 3 // safe to retry when idempotent
  }
} else {
  // existing defaults with expo+jitter
}
```
This preserves user ergonomics for idempotent flows while preventing accidental duplication.

amy_billing: Also recommend adding server-side heuristic: if duplicate charge requests from same device token arrive within X ms and no idempotency key, queue for human review or apply low-level dedup by request fingerprint (amount + card fingerprint + client nonce) for a short window. Not a substitute for idempotency keys but helps emergency mitigation.

lina_support: Customer asked for short-term mitigation they can do today. Suggested: 1) Upgrade to latest SDK pre-release (we can push patch), 2) Add client-side rate limiter to space retries (full jitter + cap), 3) Add Idempotency-Key for payments. They said they can do 3 quickly.

mike_sre: Also log note: we saw a pattern where client backoff used linear backoff (fixed 300ms -> 300ms -> 300ms) which aggravated burst. Recommend exponential backoff with full jitter (AWS/Exponential-Full-Jitter doc). Example timings: base=200ms, max=2s, randomized between 0..base*2^n.

jess_sdk: I'll open an SDK PR to: change default retry-on-429 behavior for non-idempotent POSTs, add opt-in config flag (allow429RetriesForNonIdempotent=true), and add runtime warning when retrying a POST without Idempotency-Key.

eli_infra: For server side, we can also add an advisory header to 429 responses in next deploy: `X-Server-Advice: use-idempotency-key` to make it explicit to clients. I can put that on the short-term patch. deploy-bot: rollout rtx/infra-burst-mitigations v1.3.2 completed :rocket:

deploy-bot: v1.3.2 deployed to prod (config flag adding X-Server-Advice on 429).

lina_support: I'll send the remediation steps to the customer and request they add Idempotency-Key immediately. Also offering to open billing dispute if duplicates already charged.

amy_billing: Please attach charge IDs and timestamps when you send to billing ops. We'll prioritize refunds for verified duplicates.

mike_sre: Follow-ups: Lina please gather a small anonymized log bundle (request ids, headers, times). Jess please link SDK PR and release notes. Eli please confirm the X-RateLimit-* values and whether we can increase burst quota for this customer while they patch.

lina_support: Will do. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

jess_sdk: Filed PR #4829 with the default-change and docs note, test matrix added.

eli_infra: Increased temporary burst allowance by +10 requests/min for org acme-pay-id=org_789 for 24h while they patch.

lina_support: Customer updated: applied Idempotency-Key on mobile, no duplicates in the last 3 hours. Marking as resolved on customer side, leaving thread open a bit for internal follow-ups. :relieved:
